execution_method: one original-resolution local visual assessment per case against the versioned rubric
pass_rule: Near-zero means <= 0.02; high means >= 0.70; low means <= 0.05; an order effect is material when any compared component changes by more than 0.05. Every required relation must pass.

cases.expected_relation: The pixel-identical Style truth candidate must have near-zero style, color, composition, and technical loss.
evidence: Candidate and Style truth are the same local PNG, so their observable palette, poster arrangement, contours, texture, and technical rendering match exactly.
The candidate depicts style-reference content rather than the source-controlled subject, producing the expected high source-fidelity and semantic losses outside this style-only relation.

cases.expected_relation: The pixel-identical Source truth candidate must have near-zero source-fidelity and semantic loss.
evidence: Candidate and Source truth are the same local JPEG, preserving the same person count, facial geometry, hairstyle, clothing, seated pose, and photographed setting.
The unstyled photograph lacks the style truth's editorial illustration, color-block palette, abstract graphics, ink contours, and printed texture.

cases.expected_relation: The unstyled source candidate must retain low source-fidelity loss while producing high style and color loss against Style truth.
evidence: The candidate is exactly the Source truth, so source-controlled person, pose, clothing, and image content visibly match.
Its photographic beige-and-gray setting has none of the style truth's high-contrast abstract color fields, navy contour illustration, brush marks, or print texture.

cases.expected_relation: Changing presentation order only, while preserving role labels, must not materially change the assessment.
evidence: With roles preserved, the identical source photograph still matches Source truth exactly and visibly lacks Style truth's editorial treatment.
No observed component changes from the cross-domain baseline.
